provenance.instrument: Camp Hill Borough Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 200 Zoning, Ord. No. 2023-04 of 4-12-2023, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 CA1048, Borough of Camp Hill, Cumberland County (200-13 'Borough': 'The Borough of Camp Hill, Cumberland County, Pennsylvania'). The borough website links its Borough Code to this eCode360 code. The use table (200-19) and the area and design tables (200-15, 200-21) are text in the codified chapter. The borough website also posts the 2023 ordinance and use table as PDFs, which were not opened. Floodplain, natural resources, heritage and design overlays are in Article VII of the zoning chapter. New Laws: five ordinances of 2026 on peddling, antidiscrimination, personnel, on-lot sewers (Chapter 168) and police interactions. None amends Chapter 200
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 05-13-2026.' New Laws lists Ord. No. 2026-01, 2026-03, 2026-04, 2026-05 and 2026-06, none of them on Chapter 200
checks: ADU: 'Accessory dwelling unit for care of relative' is an accessory use in LDR, MDR, MDRO and MDRO1. A unit 'Not involving a new detached accessory building' is permitted by right. A unit 'Involving a new detached accessory building' is a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board (200-19B(1)(a)). The Park district reads N (not permitted). The table of nonresidential districts (CS, CG, DT, CN, LIN) does not list it, and a use not listed in a district is prohibited there (200-19B, C)

Who may live there: 'No more than two persons, who shall be close relatives of the owner of the principal single-family dwelling unit'. At least one must need care, such as an elderly person (generally 62 or older), a special needs adult or a person with a disability (200-101E). The owner must live on the premises (200-101D). The owner renews the permit each year on proof that a relative still lives in the unit (200-101M)

The unit must be designed so it can easily become part of the house again, with a written plan for that, and a legally binding mechanism must stop its use as a separate dwelling unit after the relative leaves (200-101F, G)
No more than two dwelling units on the lot in all (200-101B). The unit has its own kitchen, bathroom and living and sleeping space and access to the outside or a common hall (200-101C)

A unit inside the house: no change to the outside except a rear addition, and no new door or wall openings except as fire and safety rules need (200-101H). Fire escapes go at the rear or side, not on a wall facing a street (200-101I). A new accessory building for the unit must match the house in design, materials, colors and roof pitch (200-101K)

'Accessory dwelling units in accessory buildings shall not otherwise occupy ground floor off-street garage floor area, to avoid displacing required off-street parking spaces provided on the lot' (200-101J)

The ADU section sets no size cap. Each dwelling unit needs at least 500 sq ft of enclosed habitable floor area, or 800 sq ft with three or more bedrooms, unless Article VIII or XII provides otherwise (200-46B). Article XII sets no other size for the ADU, so this minimum reaches it. Habitable floor area leaves out bathrooms, closets, halls, storage and utility space (200-13), so the whole unit is larger

Accessory buildings: up to 25 ft or 2 stories, not in the front yard, 3 ft from side and rear lot lines, 5 ft from the house or else attached and counted as part of it (200-15 Tables, Note A, 200-36B). At most two accessory buildings on a house lot, and 'The gross floor area for all accessory buildings and similar structures shall not exceed 50% of gross floor area of the principal building' (200-36C(1)(a), (b))

Parking: 'Accessory dwelling unit for care of relative: 2 per dwelling unit as part of principal use, plus 1 per accessory dwelling unit' (200-79 Table 9-9). The ADU section waives the ADU's space if the applicant shows by credible evidence that its residents will not routinely drive (200-101L)

The area tables give the lot area 'per DU' (6,000 sq ft in LDR, 5,000 sq ft in MDR, MDRO and MDRO1). One reading counts the ADU as a second dwelling unit (200-101B), so 12,000 or 10,000 sq ft. The stronger reading is that it does not count: the accessory use column says accessory uses are 'Included as part of total minimum lot area for principal use', a two-family dwelling needs only 4,000 sq ft per unit, and doubt is read in favor of the owner (200-4A). So the figure is shown as a point to ask about, never as a bar

'Accessory apartment' is defined as a unit on an owner-occupied single-family detached lot (200-13), but the use table lists accessory apartments only with an allowed principal commercial use in DT and CN, and the standards are for that case (200-100A, 350 to 1,200 sq ft). So it is not a path for a house lot

Apartment conversion: in MDRO and MDRO1 a special exception, only in a building that existed when the chapter was adopted (4-12-2023) with at least 3,000 sq ft of 'indoor heated living floor area' (200-19 note *), or 3,000 sq ft of habitable floor area (200-95A(1)), with no added floor area, footprint or height. A two-unit conversion meets the two-family dimensional rules. Each unit at least 500 sq ft under 200-46, 600 sq ft under 200-95A(6). No unit in an accessory building except a unit for care of a relative (200-19 note *, 200-95A, 200-46). Two parking spaces per unit (200-79)

Two-family detached dwellings are permitted by right in LDR, MDR, MDRO and MDRO1 (200-19). That is a new building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is an apartment conversion. In LDR and MDR a lot holds one principal structure (200-52B), so a two-family building takes the place of the house. In MDRO and MDRO1 a lot may hold more than one permitted principal structure if all other rules are met (200-52A), so a two-family building or a second single-family detached dwelling may stand beside the house on a lot big enough for both

Floodplain Overlay (200-29): a permit for any construction or development. In the floodway no structures except bridges, culverts and the like, and the permitted uses there 'do not include buildings' (200-29C(2)(a)[1], [4]). In an AE zone without a floodway, no new construction or development within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft), and basements are prohibited. An accessory structure that is not elevated may not be designed or used for human habitation and may have no sanitary facilities (200-29D(2)(e))

Floodplain new construction: 200-13 counts a structure begun on or after March 10, 1977 as new construction, with 'any subsequent improvements thereto'. 200-30 uses the start date of the floodplain ordinance. Where the chapter conflicts, the more restrictive provision applies (200-29A(4)). So an addition to a house begun after March 10, 1977 may need full elevation. For an older house the work is an improvement, and full compliance is needed at 50% or more of its market value (200-29G(2)(c)). Ask the Floodplain Administrator

Floodplain variances are decided by the Zoning Hearing Board on exceptional hardship (200-29H(1)). 'No variance shall be granted for any construction, development, use, or activity within any floodway area/district that would cause any increase in the BFE' (200-29H(2)(a)[1]). 'No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size', and a signed non-conversion agreement is a condition of any such variance (200-29H(2)(a)[3]). No variance for the prohibited activities of 200-29F (200-29H(2)(a)[5])

Natural Resources Overlay (200-34): on natural slopes of 25% or more no structures, and limits on how much of a 15% to 25% slope may be disturbed. No buildings within 25 ft of the ordinary waterline of a perennial creek, and no structures within 25 ft of a non-tidal wetland

Heritage Conservation Overlay (200-33): a new principal building is a conditional use. Removing or covering historic details, or closing an original window or door visible from a street, on a principal building in the overlay built before 1-1-1945 is a partial demolition and needs conditional use approval from Borough Council. No approval is needed for interior work or for removing features, such as a rear porch, that do not harm the structure and are not visible from a public street, or features added after 1-1-1945 (200-33C(5))

Development Compatibility Overlay (200-32): design standards for the features an application touches, such as front windows and doors, porches, fire escapes and garages. In DT, residential garages go behind the rear wall of the house

Nonconforming lot of record: a lot of record held apart from the abutting lots may be used for a permitted use though it is below the minimums (200-89A). The Zoning Officer may cut side or rear yards by up to 25% for a lot that lacks width or depth, and more needs the Zoning Hearing Board (200-89B(2)). A nonconforming structure may grow by up to 25% of its floor area if no new nonconformity results, and an addition may follow an existing nonconforming yard line (200-90B)

Each lot in a residential district (LDR, MDR) has one principal use and one principal structure unless the chapter permits more (200-52B). A lot in MDRO, MDRO1, DT, CN, CG or LIN may have more than one permitted principal use or structure if all other requirements are met, and the most restrictive rule applies where they differ (200-52A)

A use not provided for anywhere in the chapter may be allowed by Borough Council as a conditional use only if it is 'Not permitted in any other zoning district' (200-4B(2)(b)). The ADU for care of a relative is permitted in LDR, MDR, MDRO and MDRO1, so this does not open it in other districts. The use table points to 200-5B for that process, but 200-5B is a public utility rule, so the reference is read as 200-4B

Vegetative coverage: at least 25% of the lot in LDR, MDR, MDRO and MDRO1 (200-15 Tables 3-2, 3-3, 200-21 Table 4-2). A new building or addition for the unit must leave it. The special exception that raises impervious cover may not overturn this minimum (Note J)

Front yard parking in MDRO and MDRO1: 'no new vehicle parking spaces shall be established between an existing or proposed principal building and the front street right-of-way line'. On a corner lot this holds along the more heavily traveled street (200-21 Table 4-2 Note A)

DT and CN permit 'Apartments, which may include a conversion' by right, but 'New apartments shall only be allowed in a building that also includes an allowed street-level principal commercial use' (200-19B(1)(b) note 1). An apartment is a unit of a multifamily dwelling (200-13). Not a path for a house alone

Airport Overlay (200-31): applications to erect a new structure, or to add to or raise the height of an existing structure, in the mapped zones around Capital City Airport and Harrisburg International Airport are reviewed under 200-31. A new building for the unit or an addition there may need that review. Read only at its start

term.value: accessory dwelling unit for care of relative
term.section: 200-13 'Accessory dwelling unit for care of relative', 200-19B(1)(a), 200-101
term.note: 'An accessory dwelling unit that is especially created for and limited to occupancy by a close relative of the residents of the principal dwelling unit, is necessary to provide needed care and supervision to such relative and meets the requirements for such use in Article XII, § 200-101'

status.note: By right in LDR, MDR, MDRO and MDRO1 when the unit does not involve a new detached accessory building, and a special exception when it does. Only close relatives of the owner, at least one of whom needs care, may live in it

scope_districts.note: The residential use table lists the unit as P or SE in LDR, MDR and 'MDRO and MDRO1', and N in the Park district

status_outside.note: 'any land or structure shall only be used or occupied for a use specifically listed in this chapter as allowed in the zoning district' (200-19B), and 'An accessory use of a dwelling is only permitted if such use is customarily incidental to the residential use and is specifically permitted by this chapter' (200-19C). The nonresidential use table (CS, CG, DT, CN, LIN) does not list the ADU. The conditional use for uses not provided for reaches only a use not permitted in any other district (200-4B(2)(b)), and the ADU is permitted in LDR, MDR, MDRO and MDRO1

value.note: The Park district column reads N, 'Not Permitted', for both rows of the accessory dwelling unit for care of relative

path.note: 'Accessory dwelling unit for care of relative' - 'Not involving a new detached accessory building': P (zoning decision by Zoning Officer). The owner renews the permit each year

value.note: 'Involving a new detached accessory building': SE, decided by the Zoning Hearing Board on the criteria of 200-118E(3)(b)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 200-118E(5)(a) to (e). No bar on a use variance

value.name: Apartment conversion (MDRO, MDRO1)
value.conditions: Conversion of an existing single-family detached dwelling that had at least 3,000 sq ft of indoor heated living floor area (habitable floor area in 200-95A) when the chapter was adopted (4-12-2023). No added floor area, footprint or height except for fire safety and disability access. A two-unit conversion meets the two-family detached dimensional rules (4,000 sq ft per dwelling unit and 80 ft wide). Each unit at least 600 sq ft, all units in the principal building, and the outside keeps its residential look. No new parking between the front of the house and the front lot line. Two parking spaces per unit. If the lot is next to Market Street, a new unit needs a street-level commercial use in the building

requires.condition: An existing single-family detached dwelling to convert
At least 3,000 sq ft of indoor heated living floor area when the chapter was adopted
The building existed when the chapter was adopted on 4-12-2023

value.note: The lot figure reads the two-family rule of 4,000 sq ft per dwelling unit as 8,000 sq ft for two units. The chapter took effect on 4-12-2023 (200-11)

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (MDR)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units, one over the other or side by side, with two side yards. 4,000 sq ft per dwelling unit and 80 ft wide (95 ft on a corner lot). Front 25 ft, side 5 ft, rear 25 ft, footprint 40%, impervious cover 60%, vegetative cover at least 25%. Two parking spaces per unit

requires.condition: A building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is an apartment conversion instead

value.note: A lot in a residential district holds one principal structure (200-52B), so in MDR the two-family building takes the place of the house

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (MDRO, MDRO1)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units, one over the other or side by side, with two side yards. 4,000 sq ft per dwelling unit and 80 ft wide (95 ft on a corner lot). Front 25 ft, side 5 ft, rear 25 ft, footprint 40%, impervious cover 60%, vegetative cover at least 25%. Two parking spaces per unit. No new parking between the house and the front street line

requires.condition: A building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is an apartment conversion instead

value.note: 8,000 sq ft where the two-family building takes the place of the house. A lot in MDRO or MDRO1 may hold more than one permitted principal structure if all other rules are met (200-52A), so the building may also stand beside the house on a lot with 5,000 sq ft for the house and 8,000 sq ft for the two units, with every yard and coverage rule met for both

value.name: Second single-family detached dwelling (MDRO, MDRO1)
value.conditions: A second single-family detached dwelling as another principal building on the lot. A lot in MDRO or MDRO1 may hold more than one permitted principal structure if all other rules are met, and the most restrictive rule applies where they differ. 5,000 sq ft per dwelling unit, so 10,000 sq ft for two houses. Each house meets the yards (front 25 ft, side 5 ft, rear 25 ft), footprint 40%, impervious cover 60% and vegetative cover 25%. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit, none new between a house and the front street line. No family, owner or care rule

requires.condition: An existing house on the lot, with the new house as a second principal building

value.note: 200-52A lets the lot hold more than one permitted principal structure 'provided all other requirements of this chapter are met'. The lot figure reads 5,000 sq ft per dwelling unit for two houses

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (LDR)
value.conditions: A building with two dwelling units, one over the other or side by side. LDR gives no two-family column, so the 'Other Uses' figures read as applying: 30,000 sq ft and 90 ft wide, front 25 ft, side 7 ft, rear 30 ft, footprint 30%, impervious cover 50%. Two parking spaces per unit

requires.condition: A building for two units. Turning the existing house into two units is an apartment conversion, which LDR does not permit

value.note: Whether the LDR 'Other Uses' column is the two-family figure is not settled

building_types.note: 'The principal use of the building and property must be a single-family dwelling.' The code defines single family detached, semidetached and attached dwellings, and the section does not name one type

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Not used as a test. Whether the ADU counts as a dwelling unit for the lot area 'per DU' is a gate condition

historic_bypass.note: The Heritage Conservation Overlay adds approvals for changes to older buildings. It gives no path for an ADU

districts_read_no_listing.note: The nonresidential use table lists no ADU. DT and CN permit single-family detached dwellings and twins, CS, CG and LIN do not

value.condition: A unit inside the house may change the outside only by a rear addition, and may add no door or wall openings except as fire and safety rules need. The house must keep resembling the dwellings in the neighborhood.
A new accessory building for the unit must match the house in design, materials, colors and roof pitch.
'Accessory dwelling units in accessory buildings shall not otherwise occupy ground floor off-street garage floor area, to avoid displacing required off-street parking spaces provided on the lot'.

A unit added over an existing garage reads as not involving a new detached accessory building, so it is by right. A garage built new with the unit over it is a new detached accessory building, which is a special exception, as for a detached new unit. With no garage on the lot, that is the path.

Each dwelling unit needs at least 500 sq ft of enclosed habitable floor area, or 800 sq ft with three or more bedrooms. Article XII sets no other size for the ADU, so this minimum reaches it. Bathrooms, closets, halls, storage and utility space do not count as habitable floor area.
On a house lot at most two accessory buildings, and the gross floor area of all accessory buildings together may not exceed 50% of the gross floor area of the house.

In the Floodplain Overlay any construction or development needs a permit. In the floodway no structures except bridges, culverts and the like, and no new construction without a DEP permit. New construction and substantial improvement of a residential structure need the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation (base flood elevation plus 1 1/2 ft), and basements are prohibited. New construction is a structure begun on or after March 10, 1977, with its later improvements (200-13), and the more restrictive provision applies (200-29A(4)). So an addition to a house begun after that date may need full elevation, and work on an older house needs it at 50% or more of the house's market value. Ask the Floodplain Administrator.

In an AE zone without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the DEP Regional Office'.

In the Floodplain Overlay a new building for the unit is a residential structure. It must be built with its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation and no basement. The exemption for accessory structures that are not elevated does not cover a building for human habitation. In the floodway the permitted uses do not include buildings, so no new building there.

no_variance.quote: No variances shall be granted for a proposed accessory structure that exceeds 600 square feet in size.
no_variance.note: A signed non-conversion agreement is required as a condition of receiving the variance

value.condition: In the Floodplain Overlay an existing garage or other accessory structure that is not elevated 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' and may have no sanitary facilities. A unit there needs the building raised and rebuilt as a residential structure with its lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation. One of 200 sq ft or more below the base flood elevation carries a recorded non-conversion agreement.

disputed_by.note: A garage that is already elevated, or is raised so its lowest floor is at or above the regulatory flood elevation and meets the rules for residential structures, is not held to the accessory structure limits

value.condition: Natural Resources Overlay: on natural slopes of 25% or more only uses without structures are permitted, and only part of a 15% to 25% slope may be disturbed (50% of slopes of 15% to 17.99%, 25% of slopes of 18% to 24.99%). No buildings within 25 ft of the ordinary waterline of a perennial creek, or on springs and slopes of 25% or more within 50 ft of it, and no structures within 25 ft of a non-tidal wetland. The applicant maps these features.

Heritage Conservation Overlay: on a principal building built before 1-1-1945, removing or covering historic details, or closing an original window or door visible from a street, is a partial demolition that needs conditional use approval from Borough Council. No approval is needed for interior work or for removing features, such as a rear porch, that do not harm the structure and are not visible from a public street, or features added after 1-1-1945.
In MDRO and MDRO1 no new parking space may go between the house and the front street right-of-way line. On a corner lot this holds along the more heavily traveled street.

The LDR table gives 6,000 sq ft of lot 'per DU'. One reading counts the ADU as a second dwelling unit, so 12,000 sq ft for the house and the ADU. The stronger reading is that it does not count: accessory uses are 'Included as part of total minimum lot area for principal use', and doubt is read in favor of the owner (200-4A). Ask the zoning officer on a smaller lot.

The table gives 5,000 sq ft of lot 'per DU'. One reading counts the ADU as a second dwelling unit, so 10,000 sq ft for the house and the ADU. The stronger reading is that it does not count: accessory uses are 'Included as part of total minimum lot area for principal use', a two-family dwelling needs only 4,000 sq ft per unit, and doubt is read in favor of the owner (200-4A). Ask the zoning officer on a smaller lot.
At least 25% of the lot stays in vegetative cover. A new building or addition for the unit must leave it, and the special exception that raises impervious cover may not overturn it.

types_allowed.note: The table names units involving and not involving a new detached accessory building, and 200-101 speaks of units within the house, rear additions and units in accessory buildings

labels.note: Only a rear addition may change the outside of the house

max_sqft.note: The ADU section sets no size cap

min_sqft.note: 'each dwelling unit shall include a minimum of 500 square feet of enclosed habitable floor area', 800 sq ft with three or more bedrooms, 'Unless otherwise provided for in Article VIII and Article XII'. Article XII (200-101) sets no other size, so it reaches the ADU. Habitable floor area leaves out bathrooms, closets, halls, storage and utility space

setback_side_ft.note: 'A three feet wide minimum side and rear setback shall apply for a permitted detached structure that is accessory to a dwelling'

setback_rear_ft.note: A vehicle garage stays at least five feet from the cartway of an alley

The owner renews the permit each year on proof that a relative still lives in the unit. A binding mechanism stops use as a separate unit after the relative leaves.

setback_front_ft.note: Note I lets an unenclosed front porch reach up to 10 ft into the front yard

setback_side_ft.note: '5 feet each side from interior lot line'. 12 ft from a street right-of-way line. A lot that existed before 8-2-1943 and is under 50 ft wide needs 4 ft, 10 ft for both (Note G)

setback_rear_ft.note: A lot that existed before 8-2-1943 with a depth under 100 ft needs 15 ft (Note H)

max_building_coverage.note: 'Building footprint - maximum'. The footprint counts the ground area of all buildings, including roofed decks and porches

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Impervious lot coverage - maximum'. A special exception may raise it up to 95% with added landscaping and stormwater proof (Note J)

principal_max_height_ft.note: '35 feet or 3 stories, whichever is more restrictive'

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: 'A three feet wide minimum side and rear setback shall apply for a permitted detached structure that is accessory to a dwelling'. A vehicle garage stays at least five feet from the cartway of an alley

accessory_setback_rear_ft.note: Three feet. A vehicle garage stays at least five feet from the cartway of an alley
